title: 开始阅读最后更新：2026-07-22 22:10:41 最新章节：第179章 十二属相一
content_zh:
天刚亮，又下起雨，细密雨线从屋瓦上划过，化为水滴淅沥沥砸在青石砖地上。到处都是雾蒙蒙的，天上挂着抹极淡的月牙，仿佛下一刻就会散去。
沈二在窸窣声中醒来，目光一扫，便见一条细小黑蛇，叼着团灰扑扑的东西从破瓦处滑进来，落到被打湿一片的木地板上。
这条蛇是前段时间，她上山偷鹰崽时，在鹰窝里捡到的小蛇。那时它奄奄一息，用少了一截的尾巴尖努力勾住她的手指，眸中满是求生的乞怜，索性就把它带了回来。
待养好伤，它就赖着不走了，在她生病期间，还经常给她带吃的回来。
小蛇叼着那半截死老鼠，献宝似的想往沈二榻上爬，被捏住后颈调转方向，“你自己留着吃吧。”
声音低哑虚弱，话音落下，一串剧烈的咳嗽随之响起。
“咳咳咳——咳——”
沈二掩唇，倾身朝向榻外，不住地干呕，连带身子都跟着颤抖。楼下，小姨刺耳的骂声穿过木地板传来：
“别咳了！大早上的就在那里咳咳咳！老娘真是倒了八辈子血霉了！招了这么个病痨鬼在家里！”
然后是姨丈带着困意的说话声：“你能不能小点声，老子都被你吵醒了。”
沈二收了声，无力地靠在墙上，光透过窗户缝隙打在沈二消瘦苍白的下颌，她这样咳了有半个月了，也不怪小姨会嫌她烦。
起初以为只是普通的风寒，但吃了药也不见好，直到遇到个算命先生，说她只剩下三个月可活，且无药可医。
一开始她是不信的，但现在，她深信不疑，而且觉得三个月还多了。
大夫说她这病不会传人，可小姨嫌她晦气，把她关在阁楼，不让她出去，一天送一次饭。
雨水从屋顶漏口处啪啪滴在木地板上，那个口子是为小蛇预留进出的，因为它不喜欢走窗户。这几天连着刮风下雨，原本的小口豁成大口，没来得及补。
沈二把架子上的木盆拿下来，放在漏口底下，让水滴在盆里，想着待会小姨送饭上来时，讨块木板碎瓦，她自己就能把屋顶补好。
她是个没爹没娘的，在很小的时候，就跟着小姨生活。小姨说，她是她娘未婚先孕生的孩子，亲爹据说是个修仙的，跟她娘一见钟情，相见恨晚。
但在她娘怀上她之后，她那个亲爹就带着剑飞走了。唯一留下来的东西是个木头簪子，上面刻着符文，据说是可以驱邪保平安。
这也是她娘唯一留下来的东西，她娘生她时难产，生下她之后便撒手人寰。
这些都是小姨告诉她的，她什么都记不得，只能通过小姨所说，在脑子里想象出一个与小姨七八分像，穿着秀丽衣裙，每天站在院子里翘首以盼的身影。

为了这么个抛妻弃子的人渣断送自己的一辈子，她真心为她娘感到不值。也因此，从心底里对那个素未谋面的亲爹生出恨意。
现在再多的恨意和不甘都无法去寻了，沈二望向一滴一滴滴入水盆的雨水，眼神逐渐涣散。
“你说说，那个死丫头哪来的狗屎运！都快死了，她那个失踪十六年的爹竟还传了信来，要接她上山修仙！”院外，小姨面红耳赤，一双眼睛瞪大，死死盯着姨丈手里的信纸，恨不得把信戳出两个洞来。
“明日就派人来接，看信上这意思，小二这爹派头不小。”姨丈咂咂嘴，“诶，说不准上了山，小二就有得救了。”
content_en:
Just after dawn, it started to rain again. Thin lines of rain streaked across the roof tiles, turning into water droplets and pattering on the bluestone tiles. There was fog everywhere, and a very faint crescent moon hung in the sky, as if it would dissipate in the next moment.
Shen Er woke up to the sound of rustling, and when he glanced around, he saw a small black snake, holding something dusty in its mouth, sliding in from the broken tiles and landing on the wet wooden floor.
This snake was a small snake she picked up in the eagle's nest when she went up the mountain to steal an eagle cub some time ago. At that time, it was dying, and it tried hard to hook her finger with the tip of its missing tail. With its eyes full of pity for survival, she simply brought it back.
After recovering from his injuries, he would not leave. During her illness, he often brought her food back.
The little snake held the half of the dead mouse in its mouth and tried to climb onto Shen Er's couch as if offering a treasure. It pinched the back of the neck and turned around, "You can keep it for yourself."
The voice was low and weak, and after the words fell, a series of violent coughs sounded.
"Cough cough cough - cough -"
Shen Er covered his lips and leaned towards the outside of the couch, retching and trembling all the time. Downstairs, my aunt's harsh curses came through the wooden floor:
"Stop coughing! You're coughing there in the morning! I'm really in trouble for eight lifetimes! I have such a sick and consumptive person in my house!"
Then came the sleepy voice of my uncle: "Can you please keep your voice down? I've been woken up by you."
Shen Er stopped talking and leaned against the wall weakly. The light shined through the gap in the window and hit Shen Er's thin and pale chin. She had been coughing like this for half a month. No wonder her aunt found her annoying.
At first she thought it was just a common cold, but even after taking medicine, she didn't get better until she met a fortune teller who told her that she only had three months to live and that there was no cure.
She didn't believe it at first, but now, she is convinced, and she feels that three months is more than three months.
The doctor said her disease was not contagious, but her aunt thought she was unlucky and locked her up in the attic, not letting her out and delivering her meals once a day.
Rainwater dripped onto the wooden floor from a leak in the roof. That opening was reserved for the little snake to get in and out, because it didn't like to go through the window. It has been windy and rainy in the past few days, and the small hole has become a big hole, and there is no time to repair it.
Shen Er took the wooden basin off the shelf and placed it under the drain, letting water drip into the basin. He thought that when his aunt brought the food later, he would ask for a piece of wood and broken tiles so that she could mend the roof herself.
She has no father or mother. She lived with her aunt when she was very young. The aunt said that she was the child of her mother before she was married, and her biological father was said to be a cultivator of immortality. She and her mother fell in love at first sight and hated each other until they met.
But after her mother became pregnant with her, her biological father flew away with his sword. The only thing left was a wooden hairpin with runes engraved on it, which was said to be able to ward off evil spirits and ensure peace.
This was the only thing left by her mother. Her mother had a difficult time giving birth to her and passed away after giving birth to her.
These were all told to her by her aunt, and she could not remember anything. She could only imagine in her mind a figure that looked exactly like her, wearing beautiful clothes, standing in the yard every day, looking forward to it.
She truly felt that it was not worth it for her mother to risk her whole life for such a scumbag who abandoned her wife and children. Because of this, I felt hatred for the biological father I had never met from the bottom of my heart.
No amount of hatred and unwillingness can be found now. Shen Er looked at the rainwater dripping into the basin drop by drop, his eyes gradually becoming distracted.
"Tell me, where did that damn girl get her shitty luck! She is almost dead, and her father, who has been missing for sixteen years, actually sent a letter to take her to the mountain to cultivate immortality!" Outside the hospital, my aunt was blushing, her eyes widened, staring at the letter in her uncle's hand, wishing she could poke two holes in the letter.
"I'll send someone to pick him up tomorrow. From what the letter says, Xiaoer's father is quite impressive." My uncle smacked his lips, "Hey, maybe Xiaoer will be saved if we go up the mountain."
